# dtcloud_elastic_ip (Data Source)

Looks up one elastic IP, by id or by address.

Address lookup is the useful half: an address is what a person knows, since it is in a DNS record or
in a firewall rule, while its id is written down nowhere outside the platform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By address -- the half that is actually useful, since an address is what is
# written down in DNS or in somebody's firewall rule.
data "dtcloud_elastic_ip" "web" {
  ip_address = "203.0.113.42"
}

data "dtcloud_elastic_ip" "by_id" {
  id = var.elastic_ip_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) ID of the elastic IP to look up. Give this or `ip_address`.
- `ip_address` (String) Public address to look up. Give this or `id`. Addresses are unique.

### Read-Only

- `assigned_id` (String) ID of the VM or load balancer the platform reports the address as assigned to.
- `assigned_to` (String) Name of that VM or load balancer.
- `assigned_type` (String) `VM`, `LB`, or empty when the address is unassociated.
- `created_at` (String) When the address was allocated, in RFC 3339 format.
- `description` (String) Description of the address.
- `device_id` (String) ID of the resource behind the port.
- `device_owner` (String) What kind of thing is behind the port, e.g. `compute:nova`.
- `fixed_ip_address` (String) Address on that port the traffic is mapped to.
- `floating_network_id` (String) ID of the external network the address came from.
- `network_name` (String) Name of that external network, as the platform reports it.
- `port_id` (String) Port the address is pointed at, empty when unassociated.
- `router_id` (String) Router carrying the traffic.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE` when associated, `DOWN` when not.
- `updated_at` (String) When it was last changed, in RFC 3339 format.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Every read costs two calls.** The list endpoint resolves an address to an id, and it is the only
  place the external network's name and the name of the machine behind the address appear
  (`network_name`, `assigned_to`). The details endpoint carries the raw fields. The API builds each
  row of that list from further calls of its own, so avoid this inside a large `for_each`.
* **An address that does not exist is an error**, not an empty result.
